blind_spots.blind_spot: ATAK-integrated visualization and TAK-enabled devices are named, but ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR compliance is never mentioned anywhere in the site or case studies
blind_spots.operator_reality: A system ingesting spaceport blast-zone and base-defense sensor data into a JADC2-adjacent command picture will eventually need an Authority to Operate on the government network it displays data from — technical TAK integration is necessary but not sufficient, and the accreditation path is invisible in their public materials.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their language optimizes for operator/commander-facing capability description (situational awareness, digital twin) rather than the acquisition/compliance audience that would need ATO/RMF proof points.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Tesseract implemented an integrated solution comprising PRISM™ hardware, MOSAIC RT™, and a custom ATAK-integrated visualization tool.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: Seven years of parallel small-dollar SBIR/OTA/DIU pursuits across five unrelated verticals (airbase, spaceport, special ops, agriculture, construction) with the team still at ~20 people
blind_spots.operator_reality: Spreading a small engineering team across this many simultaneous pilot programs is exactly the valley-of-death risk pattern: none of the individual programs may get the sustained engineering attention needed to convert from prototype demo to a funded program of record before its period of performance runs out.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Each new program (SWARM/USSOCOM 2024, CADDS/DIU 2026) is announced as a standalone press release without any public statement of which single line of business is being prioritized for transition.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Tesseract Ventures Announces Revolutionary SWARM Drone Technology for Special Operations Forces' (2024) alongside 'Tesseract Ventures Selected by Defense Innovation Unit for Containerized Autonomous Drone Delivery System (CADDS) Prototype Project' (2026)

blind_spots.blind_spot: The only degraded-comms acknowledgment is a 'low bandwidth' base station — no discussion of fully denied/intermittent comms, and no mention of who trains operators or sustains badges/base-stations (batteries, spares, GFE integration) in the field
blind_spots.operator_reality: A rugged badge and TNet base station deployed at an active airbase or spaceport needs a sustainment plan — dead batteries, damaged badges, and untrained new personnel are the day-to-day reality that determines whether the 'centralized source of truth' pitch survives contact with an actual operating base.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Case studies describe outcomes (real-time tracking, situational awareness) in benefit language but stop short of describing the operations-and-maintenance model behind the hardware.
